_meta.subject: Get24 — competitive real-time multiplayer math game
_meta.behavioral_safety_net: 18/18 tests passing (not modified by this analysis)
_meta.grounded_in: Direct source inspection of all files at baseline commit
_meta.note: No metrics, coverage percentages, or vulnerability scores are invented. Every claim traces to a specific file and line.

repository_overview.name: Get24
repository_overview.description: A competitive real-time multiplayer math game. Players race to submit an arithmetic expression using four given digits that evaluates to 24.
repository_overview.confirmed_broken_on: Node.js 20 LTS (server fails to boot — see F-02, F-06)

source_files.role: Application entry point — delegates to server/index.js
HTTP server setup (Express 3), Socket.IO 0.9 setup, connection management, capacity guard
Game logic: UUID room creation, timer lifecycle, expression validation, win/loss/timer round-over events
Reusable interval-based countdown timer — tick callback + final callback, looping
Card dataset: easy / med / hard arrays of 4-digit strings
Game config: maxPlayers (4), initialTimer (300), difficulty cutoffs
Client-side Socket.IO event wiring — connects and delegates to StageController
Client-side KineticJS canvas UI — splash screen, game card animation, timer/player display, round-over messaging

runtime_and_dependency_findings.reason_0_12_fails: Floating transitive debug dependency ships ES6 syntax that Node 0.12 cannot parse
runtime_and_dependency_findings.reason_node_20_fails: Express 3 app.configure() removed in Express 4; Socket.IO 0.9 io.configure()/io.set() removed in Socket.IO 1.x

direct_dependencies.name: socket.io
direct_dependencies.note: socket.emit, socket.on, socket.broadcast, socket.join APIs preserved through Socket.IO 4

direct_dependencies.name: node-uuid
direct_dependencies.output_format_change: none — UUID v4 format is identical

direct_dependencies.name: node-expression-eval
direct_dependencies.api_change: require('node-expression-eval') → require('expr-eval').Parser; new Parser() instance; evaluate() method same
direct_dependencies.risk_note: Core game mechanic — expression evaluation and error behavior must be verified

client_side_dependency.name: KineticJS
client_side_dependency.api_change: Close but not identical — shadowOffset array→object, some Tween/Animation property names differ

architecture.pattern: Monolithic single-process Node.js server + static single-page client
architecture.server_startup: index.js → require('./server') triggers immediate HTTP listen as a side-effect of module load
architecture.http_layer: Express 3.0.6 — serves static assets from public/, no dynamic routes beyond static file serving
architecture.realtime_layer: Socket.IO 0.9.19 on same HTTP port — all game state flows over socket events
architecture.game_state: In-process global arrays (gameList, numConnections) — no database, no persistence, no session store
architecture.game_rooms: Each Game instance owns a UUID v4 room ID; Socket.IO rooms used for scoped broadcast
architecture.timer_mechanism: setInterval-based countdown per game room — looping, 300s default
architecture.expression_evaluation: Server-side only — client sends raw string; server validates, evaluates, broadcasts result
architecture.capacity_guard: server/index.js accept() — emits overCapacity and immediately disconnects (race condition: advisory packet often discarded before client reads it — captured as known legacy behavior in tests)

socket_event_contract.note: All nine event names and payload shapes are locked by the behavioral safety net. Any modernization step must preserve every key listed here exactly.

server_to_client.covered_by: game-events.test.js (advisory only — packet may be discarded by legacy disconnect race)

findings.title: Node.js engine declared as 0.8.x; only functional on 6.17.1
findings.detail: The declared engine is 10+ years end-of-life. Confirmed functional only on Node 6.17.1 via Docker. Fails on Node 20 due to Express 3 and Socket.IO 0.9 incompatibilities.

findings.title: app.configure() removed in Express 4 — hard boot failure
findings.detail: app.configure() and app.configure('development', fn) have no Express 4 equivalent. Calling either throws immediately on Express 4+. Both middleware registration and dev error handler are wrapped in these calls.

findings.title: express.favicon() removed in Express 4
findings.detail: Bundled middleware removed. Replaced by the standalone 'serve-favicon' npm package. Currently serves a default favicon; no behavioral test asserts its content beyond a 200 status.

findings.title: express.logger() removed in Express 4
findings.detail: Dev request logging middleware. Replaced by the standalone 'morgan' npm package. No behavioral tests assert log output.

findings.title: express.errorHandler() removed in Express 4
findings.detail: Dev error pages middleware. Replaced by the standalone 'errorhandler' npm package. No behavioral tests exercise error responses.

findings.title: io.configure() removed in Socket.IO 1.x — hard boot failure
findings.detail: io.configure('development', fn) and io.configure('production', fn) throw on Socket.IO 1.x+. CORS origin configuration done via io.set() must be replaced with the cors option on the Socket.IO constructor.

findings.title: io.set('origins') hardcodes defunct Nodejitsu URL
findings.detail: Production CORS origin is set to http://get24.jit.su:80 — a PaaS that shut down in 2015. On Socket.IO 4 this must be an explicit cors option. Currently only works because the test harness uses xhr-polling with a localhost origin that passes the legacy substring whitelist check.
tests_protecting: socket.test.js (harness uses xhr-shim to bypass this)

findings.title: socket.disconnect() API changed in Socket.IO 4
findings.detail: In Socket.IO 4, socket.disconnect(true) is required to force-close the underlying transport. socket.disconnect() without the flag only closes the namespace. Used in the capacity guard accept() function.

findings.title: socket.io@0.9.x is end-of-life
findings.detail: socket.io 0.9.19 is the installed version. Upgrade to socket.io@4.x required for Node 20. The io.configure()/io.set() pattern is the only breaking API surface — socket.emit, socket.on, broadcast, join are preserved through 4.x.
findings.blast_radius: server/index.js (config block), package.json, public/js/SocketController.js (io.connect API changed to io(...))

findings.title: express@3.0.x is end-of-life
findings.detail: express 3.0.6 is the installed version. Upgrade to express@4.x required for Node 20. The app.configure() wrapper and all inline express.* middleware are the breaking surface; routing and static file serving APIs are preserved.

findings.title: node-uuid@1.4.x deprecated — renamed to uuid in 2014
findings.detail: node-uuid is no longer maintained. uuid@9.0.1 is the official continuation. API change is two lines. UUID v4 output format is byte-for-byte identical. Confirmed loadable on Node 6.17.1 per PLAN.md compatibility check.

findings.title: node-expression-eval@0.1.x unmaintained since 2013
findings.detail: No releases since 2013. expr-eval@2.x is the maintained continuation of the same codebase. Import path and Parser instantiation change; evaluate() method signature is identical. Risk is that any difference in operator precedence or error type would break the core game mechanic.

findings.title: Server start is a module side-effect — untestable without spawning a child process
findings.detail: require('./server') triggers HTTP listen immediately. The existing test harness works around this by spawning a child process with -r preload.js. Wrapping startup in an exported start() function would allow the harness to require and start the server programmatically, enabling faster test execution and cleaner teardown.
findings.tests_protecting: all 18 (harness currently uses child_process.spawn to work around this)

findings.title: Global mutable gameList and numConnections — cannot reset between tests
findings.detail: Process-level game state means tests must spawn fresh server processes (which they currently do). If the server is ever refactored to allow in-process testing, this global state would cause test pollution unless encapsulated.
findings.tests_protecting: all 18 (currently isolated by child process per test)

findings.title: setInterval not cleared on process exit
findings.detail: The timer's setInterval handle keeps the Node.js event loop alive after the server is stopped, preventing clean process exit in tests. The SIGINT handler in server/index.js calls process.exit() directly, masking the leak in dev. Harmful during programmatic test teardown.

findings.title: helpDialog.toggle() references undeclared variable 'layer' — ReferenceError at runtime
findings.detail: The help dialog toggle function calls layer.add(helpDialog) where layer is not declared in the enclosing scope. The correct variable is activeLayer. Clicking the Help button in the browser throws ReferenceError: layer is not defined. This is an upstream bug in the original source.

findings.title: blink || true forces blink unconditionally — showEvaluatedText parameter ignored
findings.detail: var willBlink = blink || true always evaluates to true regardless of the caller's argument. showRoundOver passes false to suppress blinking on the losing player's expression, but this is silently ignored. Upstream bug.

findings.title: validate() receives untrusted socket data without type guard — TypeError on non-string input
findings.detail: The submitExpression handler passes data.expression directly to validate() which calls String.prototype.search() on it. A malformed client sending a non-string payload would cause an uncaught TypeError in the handler. Guard: typeof data.expression !== 'string' already present at line 61, but this should be the first check before validate() is called.

findings.title: README and server/config.json disagree on default port (3001 vs 4000)
findings.detail: server/config.json sets port 4000; README says 3001. The PORT environment variable wins at runtime; the test harness uses a dynamically allocated free port. No code is broken.

findings.title: KineticJS 4.6.0 abandoned — superseded by Konva.js in 2015
findings.detail: Bundled locally at public/js/kinetic-v4.6.0.min.js. No CDN, no security updates. Konva.js is the maintained fork. API is close but not identical: shadowOffset takes an array in KineticJS vs an object {x,y} in Konva; some Tween/Animation property names differ. http.test.js asserts the filename and the string 'Kinetic' in StageController.js, so those tests would need updating.

findings.title: Hard-coded Nodejitsu production origin — defunct PaaS
findings.detail: The production origin whitelist points to http://get24.jit.su:80. Nodejitsu shut down in 2015. In a real deployment this must be replaced with an ORIGIN environment variable. No test exercises the production io.configure block.
findings.blast_radius: server/index.js line 55 — affects production deploy only

findings.title: No package-lock.json committed — floating version ranges may resolve differently over time
findings.detail: package.json uses floating ranges (0.9.x, 3.0.x). Mitigated by legacy/get24-baseline/repro/npm-shrinkwrap.json which captures the exact resolved versions (Express 3.0.6, Socket.IO 0.9.19, etc.).

recommended_modernization_order.rationale: Negligible risk, improves server stability. One line. No dependency changes. Fastest to verify.
Low risk, drop-in replacement. Two lines. UUID format identical. Easy win on dependency hygiene.
Medium risk because it touches core game mechanic, but isolated to one module. Must verify evaluation and error paths carefully.
Enables cleaner test setup for future steps. No behavioral change. Low-medium risk on startup ordering only.
Express 4 is prerequisite for Node 20 boot. Mechanical but touches entire middleware registration block. Must not be combined with step 6.
Highest-risk step. Test harness must be updated in tandem with the server. Best demo candidate: shows the full Verify → Rollback cycle clearly.
Client-only, no server behavioral risk. Done last because it has no server test coverage and requires manual browser verification.

demo_recommendation.reason: Socket.IO 0.9 → Socket.IO 4 is the most visible and narratively compelling modernization: (1) show legacy server failing to start on Node 20, (2) show the upgrade applied, (3) show all 14 socket/game-event tests passing on Node 20, (4) deliberately break an event name to show a test failure, (5) git revert to demonstrate the Rollback → Recover workflow. All nine event names and payload shapes are locked by behavioral tests, making pass/fail unambiguous.
